title: Procedures for Abattoir Sanitising and Personal Hygiene

lessons.title: Your work experience: hygiene every day
lessons.html:
What this work experience is about

In this module you work in a real pork abattoir under a mentor or supervisor. You must show, again and again, that you follow the hygiene and sanitising procedures of that abattoir. Your mentor watches you and signs your logbook when you do each task correctly.

Personal hygiene you must show every shift

  1. Arrive clean and change into clean protective clothing in the change room.
  2. Put on your hairnet (and beard net if needed) before your overall, so hair does not fall on clothing.
  3. Remove all jewellery, watches and loose items. Keep nails short and clean.
  4. Wash hands and arms at the hand-wash basin before entering the work area.
  5. Walk through the boot wash or clean your boots at the boot station.
  6. Wash hands again after the toilet, after breaks, after touching your face or phone, and whenever they get dirty.
  7. Cover any cut with a blue waterproof plaster and a glove, and report it.
  8. Report illness before your shift.

Behaviour in the work area

  • No eating, drinking, smoking, chewing or spitting.
  • Do not leave the work area in your protective clothing. Take off your apron before going to the toilet or canteen.
  • Stay in your area (dirty or clean). Follow the plant rule if you must cross.

Your mentor will check these things without warning. Hygiene must be a habit, not something you do only when someone is watching.

lessons.title: Sanitising tasks you will do
lessons.html:
Tasks on the job

During your work experience you will help with the cleaning and sanitising of the abattoir. The tasks may include:

  • Keeping hand-wash basins stocked with soap and paper towels.
  • Checking that knife sterilizers are full and hot, and reporting any that are not working.
  • Removing hair, fat and meat scraps from floors during the shift and putting them in the right bins.
  • Clearing drain covers.
  • Rinsing and cleaning tables, trays, hooks, gambrels and offal containers.
  • Helping with the end-of-shift clean: dry clean, pre-rinse, detergent, scrub, rinse, inspect, sanitise.
  • Cleaning protective equipment such as aprons, gloves and boots.

Doing it the abattoir's way

Every abattoir has written Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for cleaning, called sanitation SOPs. They tell you which chemical to use, how much, which tools, and in what order. Ask your mentor to show you the SOP for each area and follow it exactly.

Chemical safety reminders

  • Wear gloves, goggles and an apron when mixing or spraying chemicals.
  • Use only the measured amount.
  • Never mix different chemicals.
  • Keep chemicals away from meat and packaging.
  • Know where the eye-wash station is.

Machine safety

Never clean a machine that is running. Machines like the de-hairer, saws and conveyors must be switched off and locked out by an authorised person. Ask your mentor if you are unsure.

lessons.title: Evidence, checks and sign-off
lessons.html:
How your work is checked

After cleaning, surfaces are inspected before production starts. This is called a pre-operational inspection. The supervisor or quality controller looks at equipment, floors and walls, and may feel surfaces or use swabs to test for germs. If a surface is not clean, it must be cleaned again before slaughter starts.

Your logbook

For this work experience you keep a logbook or portfolio of evidence. It usually includes:

  • The date, area and tasks you did each day.
  • Cleaning checklists you completed and signed.
  • Your mentor's signature confirming you did the task correctly.
  • Comments from your mentor on what you did well and what to improve.
  • Any incident you were part of, such as a chemical splash, and what was done.

Tips for good evidence

  1. Fill in your logbook on the same day, while you remember.
  2. Write what you did in your own words, for example: 'Cleaned the scalding area: removed hair, rinsed, applied foam detergent, scrubbed, rinsed, sanitised.'
  3. Ask your mentor to sign when the task is done, not days later.
  4. Never write that you did a task you did not do.

What the mentor looks for

AreaCompetent when you
Personal hygieneFollow all hygiene rules every day without reminders
CleaningFollow the SOP steps in order and leave surfaces visibly clean
ChemicalsMix correctly and wear protective equipment
RecordsComplete checklists honestly and on time

Key points

  • Hygiene must be a habit every shift, not only when watched.
  • Follow the abattoir's sanitation SOPs exactly.
  • Never clean a running machine.
  • Surfaces are checked before production starts and must be re-cleaned if dirty.
  • Keep your logbook up to date, honest and signed by your mentor.
